picks.excerpt: iRobot launched five new self-emptying Roomba robot vacuums priced at or under $1,000 — its first U.S. products since bankruptcy and acquisition by Picea Robotics. The flagship Roomba Max 775 pairs LiDAR mapping and camera obstacle avoidance with a self-cleaning mop dock for 'fully hands-free' operation.
picks.rationale: Major fresh hardware launch — iRobot's post-bankruptcy comeback with LiDAR + camera-AI Roombas under $1,000; strongest consumer-robot anchor of the day.

picks.excerpt: A leaked Galaxy Glasses manager app reveals Samsung's AI eyewear will run One UI XR and integrate with Galaxy watches and rings for gesture control. The glasses, built with Google, Qualcomm, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, are expected at the July 22 Unpacked.
picks.rationale: Best look yet at Samsung's Gemini-powered glasses ahead of the July 22 Unpacked; kept the original SamMobile leak, dropped Tom's Guide coverage of the same story family.

picks.excerpt: Apple says the iOS 27 public beta arrives this month, bringing the waitlisted Siri AI revamp to a much wider pool of devices ahead of the fall release.
picks.rationale: Freshest, broadest angle of the overlapping iOS 27 / Siri AI cluster (chosen over Engadget supported-models and 9to5Mac beta 3) — the rebuilt Siri reaches the public this month.

picks.excerpt: Nothing unveiled the $99 Ear (3a) true wireless earbuds with up to 45dB ANC and 42 hours of battery life. Each earbud carries three microphones with AI-powered noise reduction for intelligent sound filtering during calls and recordings.
picks.rationale: Same-day product launch with concrete specs and an AI noise-reduction hook; adds the earbuds/audio sub-topic no other pick covers.

picks.excerpt: Notebookcheck reviews the Microsoft Surface Pro OLED 2026, the flagship Copilot+ convertible with Qualcomm's Snapdragon X2 Elite SoC and OLED panel — a look at how far Arm-based NPU AI PCs have come.
picks.rationale: In-depth review of the flagship Copilot+ convertible on Snapdragon X2 Elite; covers the on-device-AI PC beat and is a distinct device from the earlier HP Omnibook card.
